headline: Sources: Something ‘has to give’ on trade market with Flyers’ winger logjam
take:
Daily Faceoff reports that something "has to give" on the trade market with the Flyers' winger logjam, with Philadelphia needing help up the middle and possibly open to moving a winger to get it done soon.

The numbers back up the need for help. PHI sits at 2-6-3 after 11 games, and has generated only 40 percent of the expected goals (a measure of chance quality) so far this season. At five-on-five that falls to 35 percent, so the team is being outplayed when the game is even. The finishing has made it worse: PHI is 8.4 goals below what its chances should have produced, which points to a lack of high-end shot quality as much as bad luck. The goaltending is the one bright spot, with 3.7 goals saved above expected, so the crease is holding up better than the skaters in front of it. On special teams, the power play is creating 0.65 expected goals per game, a modest figure, while the penalty kill allows 0.66 per game. Adding a center to convert a surplus of wingers would address the weakest part of the team, but only if that center helps tilt the five-on-five play.
